newsitem.title: UK: UK FUND MANAGERS RAISE CASH LEVELS - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: UK FUND MANAGERS RAISE CASH LEVELS - SURVEY.

text.p: British fund managers raised their cash levels for the first time in a year in July amid expectations global stock markets will fall during the next three months, a survey showed on Monday.
"This month, for the first time since 1994, we are advising UK pension funds to overweight cash," global strategist Bijal Shah at Merrill Lynch.

Conducted by Gallup for investment bank Merrill Lynch on August 4 to 6 -- a day before the Bank of England raised official interest rates to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent -- the survey also revealed that fund managers continued to favour gilts over stocks.
Gallup asked 68 leading British institutions controlling funds of 1,093 billion stg about their outlook for the economy and their asset allocation plans.
"Respondents are keen sellers of UK equities, with sellers outnumbering buyers by 12 percent," the survey said. "In contrast, buyers of gilts outnumbered sellers by 22 percent."
Only a quarter of fund managers said they expected British economic activity to be stronger a year from now, down from 32 percent last month.
The growing conviction that the British economy would cool down may explain why managers were shifting their portfolios into gilts and away from British stocks, Merrill said.
Yet respondents said they expected British base rates to rise to 7.4 percent a year from 7.0 percent now.
"In our view, with Continental European activity accelerating, UK growth and base rates could go higher than most of these managers are expecting," Shah added. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
